_comment: Snapshot of `node scripts/count-tokens.mjs --snapshot`. Every number here is counted from the `f` binary's own output or from a real store — none is typed by hand. docs/content/index.md quotes these figures; regenerate this file rather than editing it.

index.note: names only, columnised grid; marginal cost is the name itself

preNamesOnlyListing.measuredFrom: git worktree of 86b3445, `npx tsx src/index.ts` (the real pre-change binary)

_encoders: o200k_base and cl100k_base agree on invocation strings and short queries; they diverge by 1-2 tokens per line on descriptions dense with slashes or hyphens. See `disagree` below rather than assuming agreement.

disagree.label: index cost per uck (grid only, average over this store)

mcpReference.note: Third-party and first-party MCP measurements, all o200k_base. Per-tool cost spans 77.6 to 963 across servers (12x), so no single multiplier describes MCP. Re-measure before quoting; see `reMeasured`.

tooltax.note: Totals from LEADERBOARD.md. The project README reports a different run (20 servers, 290 tools, 73,323 tokens), so totals move between runs — cite the dated leaderboard, not a total.

reMeasured.command: npx tooltax score npm:<package> (cmd:'...' for servers needing args)

conventions.tooltax: its own CLI, run against a live server over stdio
conventions.billed: our count of the same captured tools/list, restricted to the four fields tooltax bills (name, description, inputSchema, outputSchema)
conventions.onWire: our count of the complete tool object, including title, annotations and execution, which a server transmits and no host forwards to a model

reMeasured.note: Filesystem reproduces tooltax exactly under the billed rule, which is the check that our capture and tokenizer agree with theirs. Playwright is 25 tokens low, a version difference rather than a method one. billed vs onWire is a ~18% gap: about a fifth of what a server sends is not what a model is charged for. An earlier version of this block reported 2,879 and 4,413 as server totals; those were onWire sums divided by tool count a second time.
